_doc: The LAG's 6-max opening ranges (M2, the LAG retune at 6-max; spec
docs/ai-dlc/specs/m2-lag-6max-retune.md section 5). Like the base spec
beside it (../lag.unopened.json), this file is NOT loaded at runtime: it is
read only by backend/tools/rr_emit.py, and its emitted nodes are pasted
into the `preflop.unopened` of the 6-max override named in `emits`.
Seats are the 6-max set: LJ, HJ, CO, BTN, SB and BB. There are no UTG seats.
BB is copied unchanged from the base spec. The tier ladder (a full-weight
core plus a one-class edge at raise 0.4) is the base spec's, because it is
the LAG's edge identity. Depths are authored per row; there is no width
scalar. `raise_pct` is the combo-weighted width the emitter produces, an
annotation the emitter never reads (test_rr_emit.py asserts it is honest).
TARGETS, frozen in docs/ai-dlc/research/bot-realism-6max/m2-lag-retune.md.
The target is the MEASURED RFI (raise first in: the share of hands the seat
opens with a raise when everyone before it has folded), not the authored
width: LJ 20, HJ 23, CO 33, BTN 50, SB 43. Source triple S3 (6-max
inferred, NL10 online, PokerStrategy 'Average Pre-flop Ranges: LAG'),
VERIFIED with M1's caveat that the page never states its format.
CALIBRATION. Widths were calibrated on pooled seeds 1-5 (6,000 simulated
6-max hands each, tools.sixmax_baseline.run_baseline), never on the judged
seed 20260926. Measured RFI comes out a little above the width at later
seats, because the players who folded before them hold weaker cards on
average; it matters most at SB, where a width of 41.00 measured 44.4.
Pooled measurement of these widths (95% Wilson interval):
Every seat's pooled RFI is within one standard error of its target, so no
width was moved further (SB's 44.4 against 43 is 0.9 standard errors).
Measured with the override's final post-flop values; RFI is a pre-flop
stat, but post-flop changes reshuffle later hands of the same seed.
SHAPE. Every seat plays all pairs and every suited ace at full weight; the
width comes off the offsuit rows first (LJ offsuit is ATo+, KJo+, QJo) and
off the bottom of the suited king-to-jack rows second. Known and accepted
by the project owner (2026-09-30): from LJ and HJ this LAG opens fewer
hands than the unchanged TAG.
